# build/wire/burned.txt — the [Alias] strings that are out of circulation forever.
#
# ⚠ HAND-WRITTEN AND REVIEWED, unlike the v*.txt manifests beside it, which are generated by
# ./build.sh Architecture --wire-record and must never be edited.
#
# docs/plan/04 § Failure and upgrade makes the alias — not the CLR name — what a silo of version N
# looks up when a silo of version N+1 sends it a payload. So retiring an alias after a release is a
# payload nothing can read, and the Wire compatibility gate in build/Build.Architecture.cs fails on
# one. A line here is how you tell the gate that a particular retirement was deliberate.
#
# ⚠ ADDING A LINE IS A DECISION ABOUT DATA THAT EXISTS, NOT A BUILD FIX. Before adding one, the
# question to answer is what happens to the payloads already written under that alias — in the
# durable tier, in a stream, in flight. "Nothing has that yet" is an answer; it has to be true, and
# it stops being true at every release. The reason belongs in the comment.
#
# ⚠ A LINE HERE IS NEVER DELETED. The gate enforces the other half — an alias on this list that the
# tree declares again fails the build, because a peer still holding a payload under it would
# deserialize into the wrong type and succeed, which is corruption rather than an error. That is
# also why there is no staleness check: an alias burned four releases ago appears in none of the
# three manifests the gate reads and its line still has to stay.
#
# One alias per line. `#` starts a comment. Blank lines are ignored.
#
# ── Nothing is burned yet, and the two candidates are the reason to read the note above ──────────
#
# CyberCloud.Core.ResourceKey and CyberCloud.Identity.VaultSecretRef were both retired on
# 2026-08-11 — see the comments at the foot of CyberCloud.Core.Contracts.Tests.WireContractTests'
# Baseline and at the head of CyberCloud.Identity.Contracts/IdentityWireTypes.cs. Neither belongs
# here. Both were retired *before* v0.1.0 was cut, so neither appears in any released manifest and
# there is no payload anywhere that names them; the window in which that was free closed with the
# tag. A line here for either would be a claim the gate would then enforce forever about an alias no
# release ever published.
#
# The next alias retired in this repository is the first line of this file.
